name: Cisco Firepower — Web C2 Beacon (Recurring Uncommon-Domain Callbacks) [host/user-scoped]
xql_query:
dataset = cisco_firepower_raw
| filter act = "Allow"
| filter cs5Label = "secIntelCategory" and cs5 = "Uncategorized"
| filter cs6Label = "URLReputation" and cs6 = "Suspicious"
| filter src != null and suser != null and dhost != null
| comp count() as beacon_count by suser, src, dhost, shost
| filter beacon_count >= 8
| alter user_name = suser, int_host = src, url = dhost, host_name = shost
description: Repeated Allowed outbound connections from one internal host/user through the Cisco Firepower NGFW to a single Uncategorized / Suspicious-reputation domain — the perimeter-firewall signature of an HTTP C2 beacon. Deliberately HOST/USER-SCOPED: it carries suser (the exact box user) and the internal client IP as alert entities so XSIAM attributes the alert to the same asset/user the Cortex endpoint alerts are keyed on, letting endpoint + network fold into one case. Gated on the Security Intelligence category (Uncategorized) + URL reputation (Suspicious) so ambient browsing to known-good sites does not match.
alert_name: Cisco Firepower — Web C2 Beacon (Recurring Uncommon-Domain Callbacks)
alert_description:
What fired: >=8 Allowed outbound connections from one internal host/user through the Firepower NGFW to a single Uncategorized, Suspicious-reputation domain within the search window — a low-and-slow HTTP C2 beacon to uncommon infrastructure.

Why it matters: a host is beaconing to rare/uncategorized web infrastructure at a regular cadence (classic C2 check-in). Assessed severity: High.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols (TA0011 - Command and Control).

Investigate:
  - Identify the internal client (host_name/int_host) and user (user_name) and the beaconed domain (url); check domain reputation, registration age, and resolution history.
  - Pivot to the endpoint on the same host/user for the process that opened the connection (correlate with Cortex agent alerts on that asset).
  - Confirm the destination is not an expected/authorized service before escalating.

TA0011 - Command and Control: T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
